classification.difficultyReason: Identify two pairs of similar triangles and combine their corresponding-side ratios to determine the crossing height.

content.prompt: Two flagpoles stand perpendicular to the ground. The first pole is $6\text{ m}$ tall and the second is $10\text{ m}$ tall. The flags are $8\text{ m}$ apart. A cable connects the top of each pole to the base of the other pole. At what height $h\text{ m}$ do the cables cross?

spec.description: Two perpendicular poles, their crossing cables and the dashed perpendicular crossing height. Decorative flag fabric is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Pole heights 6 m and 10 m; horizontal separation 8 m; each cable joins one pole top to the opposite base.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and the unknown h appear in the question.

answer.short:
$h=\dfrac{15}{4}\text{ m}$.

Use corresponding-side ratios for the two cables.
answer.worked:
Let $x\text{ m}$ be the horizontal distance from the first pole to the point directly below the crossing. Each small right triangle is similar to the corresponding triangle spanning the poles (AAA similarity).
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{h}{10}&=\frac{x}{8}\\
x&=\frac{4h}{5}
\end{align*}$$
For the other cable,
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{h}{6}&=\frac{8-x}{8}\\
\frac{h}{6}&=\frac{8-4h/5}{8}\\
40h&=240-24h\\
64h&=240\\
h&=\frac{15}{4}\text{ m}.
\end{align*}$$
